title: The Dow Dove 396 Points Because the Carving Started Early
text:

https://www.barrons.com/articles/the-dow-dove-396-points-because-the-carving-started-early-1542667706 The Dow Dove 396 Points Because the Carving Started Early By Nov. 19, 2018 5:48 p.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
Red Monday. Stocks tumbled Monday, and old worries filled the news void in the holiday-shortened trading week. All three indexes suffered materially by the end of the day, with technology being the worst-performing sector. Amid fed-rate worries, trade uncertainties, and the lower home-builder sentiment, even record-high buybacks couldn’t lift the market. In today’s After the Bell, we… …look into the FAANGs’ bear market; …explain what it means to break lower than the 200-day moving average; …and speculate where oil price and energy stocks might go from here.
The Bear Eats Tech
Tech stocks caught the worst of it in the market rout.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled 395.78 points, or 1.6%, to 25,017.44, while the S&P 500 fell 45.54 points, or 1.7%, to 2690.73, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 219.40 points, or 3.0%, to 7028.48. Words like market 'selloff', 'crash', 'meltdown', and 'correction' have been bandied about by traders and analysts in ways that can make investors cringe. Here's what you need to know.
Apple (AAPL) slid 4.0% on Monday amid concerns over iPhone demand, and is flirting with bear territory . Alphabet (GOOGL) is already in it. Facebook (FB) lost 5.7% under leadership scrutiny.
Over 40% of S&P 500 stocks have fallen more than 20% from peak to trough, although the index itself was down only 12% at its lowest moment in October, according to Michael Wilson of Morgan Stanley . This is the trail left by the rolling bear market this year, which has now run its course through most corners of the market and left no sector unscathed at this point.
Major indexes–including the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Russell 2000–have all broken the their 200-day moving averages, a sign of a future downtrend. “Historically, when the 200-day moving average turns down it typically takes months, if not longer, to turn up again.” writes Wilson in a note on Monday. Wilson isn’t banging the drum to buy. He suggests that investors consider selling rallies rather than buying dips.
The good news is that Wilson believes 90% of the valuation damage is done already and the risk from here on will be much more concentrated at the stock level, especially those high-flying ones “that do not deserve a valuation premium but have simply benefitted from a crowding effect,” he writes.
After entering a bear market and a 12-day losing streak last week, the West Texas Intermediate crude oil price rose 1.3% to $57.17 on Monday as market waits for potential production cuts from OPEC countries at their expected meeting next month.
John Lynch from LPL Research thinks oil is oversold enough and might be due for a bounce. “The recent drop in oil prices is especially surprising when considering the industry has significantly cut capital spending in the years following the oil downturn in late 2014-early 2015,” notes Lynch in a Monday research report. Newsletter Sign-up
How will energy stocks act, however, is still uncertain. Oil was rallying in the first half of the year, but energy stocks didn’t . “Energy stocks have been surprisingly disconnected from oil prices for a couple of years now,” writes Lynch, who points out that the relative performance of the S&P 500 Energy Index versus the S&P 500 has not improved from mid-2017 through summer of 2018 despite the surge of crude-oil price.
A silver lining: If oil prices continue to drop, American consumers will be saving quite a bit at the pump for Thanksgiving travel.
The Hot Stock
Helmerich & Payne (HP) topped the S&P 500 Monday, thanks to a trio of analyst upgrades.
Helmerich & Payne rose $1.77, or 2.8% to $64.36.
The oilfield-services firm was upgraded to Buy from Hold by Citigroup, to Buy from Sell by SunTrust Robinson Humphrey, and to Neutral from Underperform by Credit Suisse. SunTrust’s Ken Sill, wrote this about his double upgrade of the stock: “High end rig demand and pricing are not slowing as we expected, and the recent correction in HP and oilfield-services shares has created a more attractive valuation and entry point.”
Year to date, Helmerich & Payne is down 0.4%.
The Biggest Loser
Nvidia (NVDA) slid to the bottom of the index on a bad day for tech overall.
Nvidia lost $19.73, or 12%, to $144.70.
Nvidia was already the worst-performing stock in the S&P 500 on Friday , following its downbeat guidance and price target cuts . However, the stock kept falling Monday , as there was little to distract from its dismal outlook during a holiday week light on data, and tech continued to take the brunt of the selloff.
Year to date, Nvidia is down 25.2%.
– Teresa Rivas
